svg.title: FP16 loss scaling: the representability window
svg.desc: Synthetic binary16 gradients 2 to minus 27 and 2 to 5 are multiplied by a common power of two. As integer power-of-two scales step from 1 to 4096 and back, the tiny gradient first becomes nonzero at S=8, while the larger gradient first overflows at S=2048. The orange zero-rounding region ends at the 2 to minus 25 midpoint, which rounds to zero under ties-to-even; nonzero rounded values begin just above it. The dotted link between the two pre-rounding points translates rigidly across the axis; their log2 separation stays 32, because a common loss scale multiplies both. Small labels beside LOW and HIGH show the rounded binary16 outcomes: 0 for underflow, OK for nonzero finite values, and INF for overflow. The plotted circles remain pre-rounding values. The status readout follows each discrete step. For powers of two, both examples are representable between 8 and 1024 inclusive. A sample nonfinite-check gate reads STEP ELIGIBLE for zero-underflow and both-finite cases (no Infs/NaNs in these two gradients), but SKIP (INF) for large-gradient overflow; eligibility is not numerical accuracy or an executed optimizer step.

g.aria-label: Common-scale translation: the two pre-rounding log magnitudes remain 32 exponents apart
Constant gap of 32 binary exponents for all common loss scales
Rounded binary16 outcomes by gradient: 0 means underflow, OK nonzero finite, INF overflow
Current loss scale and observed representability
Schematic finite-gradient gate: zero underflow does not trigger a nonfinite skip, but infinity does
